primary_driver: Middle East expansion and Gulf energy/shipping coupling
primary_stabilizer: Active Ukraine diplomacy and continued U.S.–China engagement

headlines.title: Middle East conflict expansion and Gulf infrastructure risk
headlines.summary: Regional attacks increasingly connect U.S.–Iran confrontation, Gulf states, energy infrastructure, shipping and global commodity risk.

headlines.title: Hormuz remains a global escalation channel
headlines.summary: Shipping disruption and threats to Gulf energy infrastructure can transmit regional conflict into energy, inflation and alliance pressure.

headlines.title: Ukraine diplomacy remains active
headlines.summary: Continued high-level diplomatic engagement is a meaningful stabilizer despite sustained battlefield pressure.

areas_to_watch.name: NATO–Russia direct engagement
areas_to_watch.why: Any sustained kinetic exchange would be a structural shift and likely cause a multi-point jump.

areas_to_watch.name: Chinese blockade or quarantine of Taiwan
areas_to_watch.why: A blockade or quarantine would create an immediate major-power alliance decision point.

areas_to_watch.name: Prolonged closure of Hormuz
areas_to_watch.why: A sustained closure would sharply increase economic-warfare and conflict-coupling scores.

areas_to_watch.name: Saudi / Gulf retaliation cycle
areas_to_watch.why: Watch whether attacks generate broader retaliation and deeper Iranian involvement.

areas_to_watch.name: Large-scale reserve or industrial mobilization
areas_to_watch.why: This remains one of the clearest differences from immediate pre-war 1939 conditions.

methodology.note: Analytical early-warning index, not a probability forecast.
methodology.formula: Weighted average of ten 0–10 factor scores, multiplied by 10 and rounded.
